Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! We can see the Afghanistan players in a huddle and they are having a long discussion about how to defend this low total. Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan are the two openers for Pakistan. Fazalhaq Farooqi has been given the new ball and is raring to go. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Pakistan will be thrilled with the job done by their bowlers and will know that they have the batting strength to breeze towards the target. The form of Babar Azam is a concern and he may be looking to get going in this game. Mohammad Rizwan will be looking to accumulate more runs in this tournament and seal their place in the final. Afghanistan were unable to defend a much higher total the last time around but the spinners have already had their off-game. The Afghans still have the ability to defend this target and put up a decent fight. Will this be a one-sided affair or will Afghanistan pull off a miraculous recovery? Do join us for the run chase shortly.

Haris Rauf (4-0-26-2) comes up for a quick word. The pacer says that Afghanistan started well but by pickings wickets, they restricted the scoring rate. Adds that bowling in the line of the stumps is always helpful in Sharjah. Praises Naseem Shah and Mohammad Hasnain for their bowling and says that the team is benefitting from their performance. Shares that his aim is to bowl the dot balls and create pressure. Hopes that they will chase down the target quickly.

Pakistan started off a bit lethargic and conceded a few loose deliveries to begin proceedings. They dropped a catch early on of Hazratullah Zazai but it did not prove to be too expensive. Pakistan got their act together soon enough and dismissed the two openers in consecutive overs. The spinners controlled the middle overs and did not allow the Afghani batters to break the shackles. Once they broke the partnership and picked up the wicket of Karim Janat, they began chipping away at the wickets regularly. The Men in Green continued bowling well till the end of the innings with all five bowlers contributing with at least a wicket. Haris Rauf picked up 2 wickets but Naseem Shah was the pick of the bowlers as he conceded just 19 runs in his full quota of four overs, taking a wicket also.

Afghanistan got off to a flier with their openers coming out with positive intent and putting on a 36-run partnership in quick time. They departed in quick succession in the Powerplay after which Ibrahim Zadran and Karim Janat began the rebuilding process. They were unable to score runs quickly but ensured that they were able to preserve their wickets. However, once the latter departed after a laboured inning, they lost quick wickets as they looked to accelerate. Ibrahim Zadran battled it out for his 35 but could not get his innings going. None of the big hitters for Afghanistan could get going but a useful cameo from Rashid Khan helped push the target close to the 130-run mark.

Pakistan have exhibited some outstanding death bowling and after the start Afghanistan had, they have done extremely well to restrict them to 129. This has been a complete bowling performance from a Pakistan side that is brimming with confidence. Afghanistan will be disappointed with the total they have on the board but will have to come out believing that they can win this game with the bowling options they have at their disposal.
Swishes and misses. Dot ball to end proceedings. A touch short and around off, at 141 kph, Khan goes back and tries to power it across the line but misses. Afghanistan finish on 129 for 6.
Short and following the batter, around leg, Rashid Khan tries to pull but gets a bottom edge and the ball travels behind to the keeper.

FOUR! BOOM! A length ball around middle, at 149 kph, Rashid Khan is fearless, he gives the charge and bludgeons it straight down the ground for a boundary. He executed the shot and knew that it was four.
SIX! This one has gone all the way! The moment there is pace on the ball, Rashid Khan capitalizes. Short and around off, at 141 kph, Rashid Khan steps back and hammers it over point for a biggie.
Another swing and a miss! This is smart bowling from Rauf. Not offering any pace. At 130 kph, he delivers it on a length and close to off, Rahid tries to slog but misses.
Swing and a miss! Haris Rauf takes the pace off and delivers it on a shortish length outside off, Khan is early into his shot and misses.
Haris Rauf to deliver the final over. There is a halt in play as Azmatullah Omarzai is receiving some treatment on the left leg.
Nails the yorker this time, on leg, Azmatullah Omarzai cannot get his bat down in time and gets hit on his foot. He looks in some pain.
Fuller one and on middle, Rashid Khan mistimes his pull shot towards deep square leg for a single.
Another slower ball, on a length and on off, Rashid Khan fails to pick it and swings way early only to connect with thin air.
A slower one now, short of a length and on leg, Azmatullah Omarzai looks to pull it away but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball goes towards square leg for one.
FOUR! A low full toss outside off, at 143 kph, Azmatullah Omarzai gives himself some room and slices it through point for a boundary.
Pakistan using the short balls well here! This is banged in on middle, Azmatullah Omarzai ducks under it. The umpire signals one for the over.
Full and on off, Azmatullah Omarzai looks to slog it but hits it with the bottom half of his bat towards third man for a run.
Mohammad Hasnain bowls another slower one, full and on middle, Rashid Khan flicks it towards short fine leg for a single.
Goes shorter and on middle, Azmatullah Omarzai pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

In the air... Falls safely! Short in length and outside off, the slower one, Rashid steps back and then has to reach out for it. He throws his bat and gets it away off the toe end. The ball flies behind cover-point and Shadab Khan scoots behind from backward point. Fakhar Zaman is sprinting forward from the deep. No calling between them. The ball eventually falls safely in between as Shadab dives. The batters get one.
A back-of-the-hand slower one, on middle, Rashid Khan looks to give the charge but only knocks it back to the bowler.
FOUR! This is a good start to the over for Afghanistan. Back of a length around off, at 143 kph, Rashid Khan rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Mohammad Hasnain is back on. 1 for 26 in his 3 overs.
Superb piece of fielding by Naseem Shah! This is short and outside off, Rashid Khan upper-cuts it to the left of the third man fielder where he does well to stop it with one hand. A single taken.
Rauf bangs in a short ball and on off, Rashid Khan doesn't pick the length early and decides to duck without looking at the ball. A friendly banter is going on between Rauf and Rashid.
Full and on middle, at 150 kph, Rashid Khan blocks it back to the bowler. Rauf picks it up and fakes a throw towards the batter, and then gives a stare to Rashid. Things are heating up!
Rashid Khan will look to take Afghanistan to a fighting total as he makes his way out to the crease.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The set batter is gone and Afghanistan are reeling. There is no substitute for raw pace. Haris Rauf hurls it across on a shortish length around middle, at 143 kph, Ibrahim Zadran stays leg-side to this one and tries to punch it through the line but gets a thick outside edge behind. Mohammad Rizwan makes no mistake and the Afghans lose their sixth wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Rizwan b Haris Rauf

Commentary.Commentary: Goes fuller and on leg, Ibrahim Zadran misses his flick and the ball loops up off his pads towards the right of the bowler.
Brilliant bouncer! This is banged short and on middle and off, Ibrahim Zadran is not expecting it and misses his pull shot.
Haris Rauf (2-0-15-1) is back to bowl at the death.
Quicker, short and on off, Ibrahim Zadran slaps it down to long off for run. 4-0-27-1, Shadab Khan has done his job.
A bit short, on middle and leg, Azmatullah Omarzai flicks it off his back foot through square leg for one.
Floated, short and on middle, turning away, Ibrahim Zadran goes back and tucks it towards mid-wicket for a run as Khan chases and fields it himself.

SIX! Dismissed! This one is in the slot and Ibrahim Zadran dismisses it from his presence. Shadab gives it a bit too much flight and lands it full and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran goes inside-out and rockets it over extra cover for a biggie.
A googly, short and on middle, turning in, Azmatullah Omarzai watches it through and flicks it towards deep square leg for one.
Quicker, full and on leg, Ibrahim Zadran drives it towards long on for a run.
Fullish delivery, on middle, Ibrahim Zadran works it towards long on for a single.
Shah takes the pace off this time. This is on a good length and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran makes room but only manages to bunt it onto the ground.
On a length and on off, Ibrahim Zadran pushes this to the left of backward point where the fielder moves to that side and cuts it out.
Fuller again and around off, Azmatullah Omarzai guides it towards third man for a run and gets off the mark.
Full and on off, Azmatullah Omarzai drives it nicely towards mid off for no run.
Azmatullah Omarzai is the new batter out in the middle and Afghanistan desperately need their tail to wag.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! A golden duck for Mohammad Nabi in his 100th T20I. Not a happy one for the Afghan skipper. Slightly short in length and around off, at 140 kph, Mohammad Nabi sticks back and goes on his toes to run it down to third man but all he manages is a bottom edge onto the stumps. Nabi is frustrated. Afghanistan are struggling. 50 wickets in T20s for Naseem Shah, becoming the youngest to do so, overtaking the evergreen and young Sahibzada Mohammad Shahid Khan Afridi!
The skipper Mohammad Nabi makes his way out to the middle and Afghanistan will be hoping for a cameo. Naseem Shah has been brought back into the attack as well.

OUT! CAUGHT! Najibullah Zadran is hunted down by Shadab Khan. The leggie has his revenge. A spinner bowls a seam-up delivery at 111 kph. It's very full and around middle, Najibullah Zadran finds it in the arc to send it out of the park but fails to hit it from the sweet spot of his bat. As a result, his shot has more height than distance and Fakhar Zaman claims yet another catch, at long on. This is a body blow to Afghanistan as Najibullah Zadran is one batter who has the ability to do all the big hitting.
Commentary.Howout: c Fakhar Zaman b Shadab Khan

Commentary.Commentary: This time it is the leg spinner, on off, turning in, Najibullah Zadran swings at it but misses.
Shadab Khan continues with the googlies, this is on middle and turning away, Najibullah Zadran tries to go for the reverse scoop but cannot connect.
BEATEN! This is another googly, on off, turning away, Najibullah Zadran looks to work it to the off side but gets beaten on the outside edge.

SIX! Najibullah Zadran flexes his muscles and hits Shadab for a biggie - first the leggie has conceded in this edition of the Asia Cup. Floated one, full and around leg, Najibullah Zadran whips it over mid-wicket and gets the correct elevation to send it over the fielder in the deep for a maximum.
A googly, short and around off, turning away, Najibullah Zadran makes room and punches it wide of deep point for a couple of runs.
Change in bowling. Shadab Khan comes back into the attack. 0 for 8 in his 2 overs so far.
On a length and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran cuts it straight to point. Only 4 runs from the over.
Back of a length and on off, Najibullah Zadran taps it towards backward point for a quick single as the fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end.
Short of a length and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran stays there and cuts it uppishly but on two bounces towards third man for one.
Goes fuller and on middle, Ibrahim Zadran makes room to clear the infield but ends up pushing it towards the fielder inside the ring at covers.
Length again and on the pads, Najibullah Zadran helps it towards backward square leg for a single.
Starts with a good-length delivery, on leg, Ibrahim Zadran flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
Mohammad Hasnain (2-0-22-1) returns to bowl, replacing Rauf.

Flighted delivery, full and on middle, Najibullah Zadran looks to smack it over extra cover but gets an inside edge. The ball rolls towards short fine leg. End of a top over and spell from Mohammad Nawaz - 4-0-23-1.
Another dot as this short delivery is tucked away towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and on leg, Najibullah Zadran knocks it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter and around middle, Ibrahim Zadran opens the face of his bat and guides it through covers for a single.
Najibullah Zadran makes his way out to the crease and with the way Karim Janat was going, this could prove to be a boon for Afghanistan.

OUT! Karim Janat holes out! Spinners had strangled the scoring rate and in an attempt to break free, Karim Janat throws his wicket away. Nawaz darts it in full, around middle at 94 kph, Karim Janat goes down low to smoke it over the leg side but it takes the toe end of his bat and balloons in the air. Fakhar Zaman, who had a tough time on the field against India, moves across to his right from long on and secures the skier safely.
Commentary.Howout: c Fakhar Zaman b Mohammad Nawaz

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle, Ibrahim Zadran eases it towards long on for a single.
A dot to end the over then! This is a slower one, on a length and on off, keeps a bit low too, Karim Janat pushes it towards backward point.
Rauf serves a yorker now, on off, Karim Janat digs it out towards mid off.
On a length and on leg, Ibrahim Zadran works this towards deep mid-wicket off the sticker part of his bat for a run.
Sharp bouncer! Rauf bangs this one short and around off, Ibrahim Zadran sways away from it.
Full and on the pads, Ibrahim Zadran tucks it towards mid-wicket and straightaway denies the single as it has gone too straight to the fielder.
FOUR! On the up and in the gap! Back of a length, around off, Ibrahim Zadran stands tall and packs a punch over extra cover for a boundary. It seems they were waiting for some pace.

Drinks break. We have reached the halfway stage and it's been some great action so far. Afghanistan started like a train on fire with their openers going on the attack straight away. Haris Rauf and Mohammad Hasnain did well to dismiss both of them and since then, the Pakistan spinners have pulled things back. Let's see how the Afghans navigate through this middle phase. Haris Rauf returns to bowl after the break.

FOUR! Much-needed boundary for Afghanistan! This is sheer power from Karim Janat. Mohammad Nawaz bowls this full around leg, Karim Janat gets his front foot out of the way and flicks the ball towards the cow corner fence for four runs.
Quicker around off, tapped towards extra cover for another run.
Flatter and on middle, Karim moves back and eases it to long on for one.
Shortish and on middle, helped to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Drifting into the pads this time on a fuller length, Karim Janat clips the ball to deep backward square leg for a single.
Mohammad Nawaz flights this one full and in line with the stumps, Karim Janat looks to flick this leg side but gets a leading edge towards cover.
Delivers this one really short and outside off, Karim Janat pulls this towards deep mid-wicket for another run. Just three runs from this over and Pakistan are building the pressure.
This one is outside off as well on a fuller length, Karim Janat blocks this to the left of the bowler.
Short once again and outside off, Karim Janat does not find the gap this time and hits the ball straight to point.
Pulls his length back and delivers this short outside off, Ibrahim Zadran slaps this towards sweeper cover for a single.
This is tossed up full and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran knocks this back towards the bowler.
Shadab Khan flights this full on middle and leg, Karim Janat clips this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! This has been beautifully placed! Mohammad Nawaz serves this one a fraction short and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran uses the crease and cuts the ball through the gap at backward point for a boundary.
Flighted full and on off, Karim Janat looks to slog-sweep but mistimes his shot to deep square leg for a run.
Mohammad Nawaz bowls this one full and in line with the stumps, Ibrahim Zadran makes room and knocks the ball to long off for a single.
Loopy and full on middle, it's wristed to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter and shorter on middle, Ibrahim Zadran goes back and punches it to long on for a run.
Fullish and around off, pushed to covers.
Shadab Khan bowls this a touch short and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran goes back in the crease and punches the ball to long off for a run.
Shadab Khan continues to flight this full and outside the off pole, Ibrahim Zadran taps this back towards the bowler.
Loopy delivery bowled full and outside off, Karim Janat taps the ball towards covers and rushes across for a single.
Bowls this a touch shorter and wide outside off, Karim Janat looks to cut but gets an under-edge. It drops in front of the keeper.
This is bowled full as well and in line with the stumps, Karim Janat pushes at this, gets an inside edge to deep square leg and they run well to take two runs.
Shadab Khan starts the over with a full delivery floated outside off, Ibrahim Zadran sends this to deep cover and takes a run.
Babar Azam going with spin from both ends now. Shadab Khan comes into the attack.

This one is full as well and just outside off, Ibrahim Zadran gets his front foot forward and hits it towards mid off. They take another quick single. 5 runs from the over and the Powerplay comes to a close, Afghanistan are 48 for 2.
Straying down leg this time on a fuller length, Karim Janat flicks this towards short fine leg and rushes for a quick run. Good rotation of strike.
Mohammad Nawaz floats this one full and outside off, Ibrahim Zadran strokes this wide of mid off and takes one.
Flights this full and in line with the stumps, Karim Janat works this wide of long on for another run.
Fires this one full and into the pads, Ibrahim Zadran clips this to deep mid-wicket and takes a single.
Mohammad Nawaz begins with a short delivery angling into the stumps, Ibrahim Zadran rocks back and knocks the ball towards cover.
We will see some spin now as Mohammad Nawaz has been introduced into the attack.
A yorker on off, Karim Janat digs it out safely to end the over.
Karim Janat walks out to bat now.

OUT! LEG STUMP IS FLOORED! Clever deception from the fast bowler. He attacks the stumps with a length ball and serves it at 119 kph. Hazratullah Zazai is bamboozled with the change in pace and fails to keep it out. It goes through his defense and obliterates the leg pole. Perhaps, there was some back pad also involved. Also, his bat had hit the back pad and that possibly prevented him from keeping it out. More than happy, Mohammad Hasnain is relieved with the wicket.
Wide! Hasnain is struggling here. Slips a length ball down the leg side and is lucky that the batter has not got any bat behind it. A good take by Mohammad Rizwan.
Mohammad Hasnain changes his angle and comes from 'round the wicket. Delivers it full and on off at 142 kph, Zazai pushes from the back foot to point.

FOUR! Poor bowling! Doesn't matter how quick you bowl, if your line is awry, you will be punished. A 143 kph delivery, on a length around leg, Zazai has no qualms in nudging it down to fine leg for a boundary. Easy pickings.
Closer to the body, on a length around leg at 145 kph, Hazratullah Zazai fails to work it around on the leg side and is hit on the pads.
Fuller and on the pads, helped to deep square leg for one.
Mohammad Hasnain is back on. He conceded 16 runs in his first over.
Fuller in length and around middle, Ibrahim flicks it to deep square leg for a single. 10 runs and a wicket from the over!
Ibrahim Zadran walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! STUMPS SHATTERED! The crowd roars and Haris Rauf is pumped up! Fast bowlers love that sight - bails flying around. Haris Rauf sticks to his line around off, on a good length at 144 clicks, Rahmanullah Gurbaz shuffles across a bit to hit it across the line but misses. The ball sneaks through and rattles the off pole.
Fullish and around off, drilled down to mid off.

PUT DOWN! Rauf goes short and serves it around off, Hazratullah Zazai tries to ramp it over third man but doesn't hey enough connection. It flies to third man and is dying down in front of the fielder, Naseem Shah tries to take it by going low but fails to grab it. The batters cross.
FOUR! Well timed and placed! Haris Rauf serves it on a length and outside off, at 147 kph, Hazratullah Zazai stays on the back foot and smashes it through point.

FOUR! Boundaries are coming thick and fast for the Afghans! A poor line from Rauf to begin his spell. Clocks 151 kph but delivers a full ball on the pads, Zazai neatly deflects it down to fine leg for a boundary.
The Afghanistan batters have forced Babar Azam to make his first change as he brings Haris Rauf into the attack.
Slower bumper around off, Zazai keeps his pull shot down and places it wide of short fine leg for one. 7 from the over!

FOUR! Finds the gap! This is brilliant batting. Shah angles across a length delivery outside off, at 144 kph, Zazai opens the face of his bat late and pierces the gap between short third man and backward point. Just used the pace of the bowler.
Shah takes the pace off this delivery. Serves it full and on middle and Gurbaz tucks it in front of square on the leg side for one.
Fuller again, around middle and leg, at 144 kph, Zazai helps it off his pads to deep square leg and takes a single.
A dipping full delivery around off, at 111 kph, Hazratullah Zazai pushes it out to mid off.
Full toss on off, Zazai hits across the line but finds mid-wicket.

SIX! Up and over the leaping fielder in the deep! Rahmanullah Gurbaz has made his intentions clear here. 16 from the over. Full in length and around middle, Rahmanullah picks it off his pads and flicks it nonchalantly over deep square leg for a maximum.

SIX! High and handsome! Rahmanullah Gurbaz is moving brilliantly inside the crease. A sharp delivery, short and angling into the batter, Gurbaz rides the bounce and muscles it over long leg for a biggie.
Gets away with a poor delivery. A length ball on middle and leg, at 145 kph, Gurbaz clips it off his pads but finds short fine leg.
Swing and a miss! Pace does the trick this time. Mohammad Hasnain clocks 145 kph as he delivers it short and wide outside off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz tries to cut but misses.

A high full toss as Mohammad Hasnain attempts a slower one. It's wide outside off at 130 clicks, Zazai slaps it down to third man and takes a single. It's called a no ball and Free Hit is coming up...
Back of a length, around off at 145 clicks, Gurbaz stays on the back foot and works it through square leg for a single. Rahmanullah Gurbaz' movement inside the crease shows that he is in form.
Wide! A 144 kph delivery, short but down the leg side, Gurbaz tries his best to pull but fails to connect.
Mohammad Hasnain starts with a half-volley around off, Rahmanullah Gurbaz drives but picks the mid off fielder.
Mohammad Hasnain to share the attack with Naseem Shah.
Timed beautifully. A touch fuller and outside off, at 144 clicks, Gurbaz drives it through the gap at extra cover. It's chased down in the deep and the batters get three runs.
Naseem Shah steams in and serves a good-length delivery outside off, at 141 kph, Rahmanullah Gurbaz stays back and pushes it to covers.

A muted appeal for an lbw, nothing from the umpire. An inswinger, full and around leg at 142 kph, Hazratullah Zazai tries to flick and gets a gentle tickle behind it. The ball races down to fine leg and Afghanistan are away with a single.
The line is a lot straighter this time, on a fuller length around off, at 143 kph, Zazai defends it back from the inner half of his bat.
Delivers it on a length and close to off, Zazai gets behind the line of the ball and pushes it to the off side.

Beaten first up! In fact, Naseem is appealing for a caught behind but doesn't get much support from behind the stumps. Considerable movement on this delivery. It lands a touch short and around off, Hazratullah Zazai stays back and pushes inside the line but gets beaten. No DRS taken, Babar Azam only claps and encourages his bowler.

We are ready for play now! We can see the players of Pakistan in a huddle. The two openers of Afghanistan, Hazratullah Zazai and Rahmanullah Gurbaz walk out to the middle now. Naseem Shah to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

We are minutes away from the start of play! But before the game begins, the umpires and the two sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Pakistan's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Afghanistan.

Mohammad Nabi, the Afghan skipper, looks a bit disappointed to lose the toss. Says that they also wanted to bowl first due to the dew factor and adds that they will now try their best to put a good score on the board. Further says that they will focus on bowling disciplined lines. Claims that it is always a tough game against Pakistan and they have played good games against them. Mentions that they don’t want to repeat the mistakes of the past and look to do things better. Informs that they have a couple of changes - Azmatullah Omarzai comes back in the XI, replacing Samiullah Shinwari and Fareed Ahmad is in for Naveen-ul-Haq.

Babar Azam, the captain of Pakistan, says that they want to bowl first due to the dew factor. Adds that the mood in the camp is cool and calm, and they want to keep that momentum. Tells that winning gives you confidence and they are looking to carry on with the same. Informs that they are going unchanged.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Hazratullah Zazai, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Karim Janat, Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi (C), Rashid Khan, Azmatullah Omarzai (In for Samiullah Shinwari), Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fareed Ahmad (In for Naveen-ul-Haq), Fazalhaq Farooqi.

Pakistan (Unchanged Playing XI) - Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Babar Azam (C), Fakhar Zaman, Khushdil Shah, Iftikhar Ahmed, Shadab Khan, Asif Ali, Mohammad Nawaz, Haris Rauf, Naseem Shah and Mohammad Hasnain.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and they have decided to BOWL first.

Pitch report - A little while back Sanjay Manjrekar was near the playing area and he started by saying that the pitches in Sharjah wear a strange dark grey look and then turn whitish grey before the game. He added that there is a typical sheen as well. Wasim Akram also joined him and reminded that it's the same strip where Pakistan thrashed Hong Kong. Akram mentioned that today's surface though is looking a lot better than the last one and in his opinion, it will be better to chase but also cautioned that chasing a 140-plus score won't be easy.
